questions.question: Direction: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. The current state of the literature / on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy / for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder / suggests that it is a promising treatment option.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

The current state of the literature / on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy / for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder / suggests that it is a promising treatment option.

options.text: on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy
options.html: on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy

options.text: for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder
options.html: for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder

options.text: The current state of the literature
options.html: The current state of the literature

options.text: suggests that it is a promising treatment option.
options.html: suggests that it is a promising treatment option.

questions.solution:
The preposition "under" is incorrect in "on the efficacy under cognitive-behavioural therapy." The correct preposition to use is "of." Of is a preposition and is commonly introduces prepositional phrases which are complements of nouns, creating the pattern: noun + of + noun. 
Example: Lima is the capital of Peru. The sentence should read "on the efficacy of cognitive-behavioural therapy." Correct sentence: The current state of the literature on the efficacy of cognitive-behavioural therapy for individuals with generalised anxiety disorder suggests that it is a promising treatment option.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

These facts should not have been disclosed for the public.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. 'for the public.'

'Disclosed for' is incorrect. 'Disclosed to someone' is the correct form. So,'for' should be replaced with 'to'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?

options.text: The old lady broke down when she heard her son lost his job.
options.html: The old lady broke down when she heard her son lost his job.

options.text: Try your level best before you decide to give up.
options.html: Try your level best before you decide to give up.

options.text: Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.
options.html: Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.

options.text: Clean out the backyard this weekend.
options.html: Clean out the backyard this weekend.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit. .

Key Points

  • The sentence "Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit." contains an incorrect use of the phrasal verb "make over".
  • The phrasal verb "make over" means to change or improve the appearance of something, which is not the intended meaning here.
  • The correct phrasal verb to use in this context is "make" or "make up", which means to arrange or tidy the bed.

Correct sentence: Make up the bed daily. It is a good habit.

Additional Information

  • Common Phrasal Verbs:
    • Break down: To lose control emotionally or mentally.
    • Give up: To stop trying or to surrender.
    • Clean out: To clean the inside of something thoroughly.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. He wouldn't let anyone to drive his new car.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.
He wouldn't let anyone to drive his new car.
questions.solution:
Option 2 is the one with the error.

Key Points

  • Let is followed by a bare infinitive (V1) in the following cases:
    Structure: Subject + let + object + bare infinitive (infinitive without 'to')
    • When 'Let' means 'allow' or 'give permission'
      Example- David's mother let him use her car.
    • When 'let' means 'allow' in the sense of 'make something possible'
      Example- This student card lets you book discount flights.
  • In passive voice too, 'let' is followed by bare infinitive
    • In the end, the hostages were let go.

Since, 'let' is used here in the sense of permission, option 2 is the right answer.

The correct sentence is: He wouldn't let anyone drive his new car.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Samurai Jack drawn his sword to exact revenge on his superiors.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Samurai Jack drawn his sword to exact revenge on his superiors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- Samurai Jack drawn​.

Key Points

  • The simple past tense is used to talk about things that happened or existed before now.
  • It shows that we are talking about something that has already happened. 
  • The structure is given below:
    • Subject + V2 + object.
  • Example:
    • ​Wolfgang entered a hula hoop contest.
  • In the given question, the act of taking the sword out has already taken place.
  • Hence according to the rule and example given above, 'drew' will replace 'drawn' in the part given in the 4th option.
     

Correct Sentence: Samurai Jack drew his sword to exact revenge on his superiors.

Additional Information

  • Some phrases are followed by past indefinite/simple tense as given below:
    • ​It's high time, It's time, It's about time, etc.
  • For example:
    • It's high time I start preparing for my final exams.
    • It's high time I started preparing for my final exams.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. Companies in countries as the United States (1)/ left out of the trade pacts could face (2)/ disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Companies in countries as the United States (1)/ left out of the trade pacts could face (2)/ disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option - 1

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. We often get confused between like & S. Like is used as preposition before noun to should relativeness. Whereas, as is used to describe function of a person or thing. Here, the United States is a proper noun and it is not performing any action. So, preposition like should be used instead of as. Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - Companies in countries like the United States left out of the trade pacts could face disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets.

questions.question: From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. Does he like to go for sight seeing when he is in holiday?
questions.questionHtml:
From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Does he like to go for sight seeing when he is in holiday?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3),i.e., In holiday?

 Explanation:

  •  The error lies in option 3, which uses the incorrect preposition 'In'.
  •  In- expressing the situation where something is surrounded by something else. Example: I am in Hawaii.
  •  Given the context, the preposition should be showing the state of his being engaged in 'a holiday'.
  •  Important Point:
  •  So, the correct preposition here should be 'On'.
  •  On- indicating the state or process that one is engaged in. Example: The officer was on leave when it happened.


Thus, the rectified sentence is: Does he like to go for sight seeing when he is on holiday?

Hinglish

  • त्रुटि option 3 में है, जो गलत पूर्वसर्ग 'In' का उपयोग करता है।
  •  In- उस स्थिति को व्यक्त करना जहां कोई चीज किसी और चीज से घिरी हो। उदाहरण: I am in Hawaii. (मैं हवाई में हूँ।)
  • संदर्भ को देखते हुए, पूर्वसर्ग को 'छुट्टी' में लगे होने की स्थिति को दर्शाना चाहिए।
  • Important Point:
  • तो, यहाँ सही पूर्वसर्ग 'On' होना चाहिए।
  •  On- उस प्रक्रिया को इंगित करना जिसमें कोई लगा हुआ है। उदाहरण: The officer was on leave when it happened. (घटना के वक्त अधिकारी छुट्टी पर थे।)

questions.question: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

options.text: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew
options.html: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'
Key Points 
  • The error is in the segment 'In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew'. The use of the definite article 'the' before 'Mount Vesuvius' is incorrect.
  • The correct expression should be 'In 79 A.D., Mount Vesuvius blew'.
  • Definite articles are not typically used before proper nouns, except in certain cases which do not apply here.
  • Use of articles before names of geographic areas, rivers, mountain ranges, groups of islands, canals, and oceans is common, but for a singular mountain like Mount Vesuvius, we don't use "the".
Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'In 79 A.D., Mount Vesuvius blew its top, burying the ancient cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.'
Additional Information
  • 'Its top, burying the ancient' and 'cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.' are grammatically correct.
  • They properly describe the event that occurred when Mount Vesuvius erupted.

Direction: Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Two border guards patrolling/the nearby frontier with Georgia have also/been reported missing from Friday night.

options.text: the nearby frontier with Georgia have also
options.html: the nearby frontier with Georgia have also

options.text: been reported missing from Friday night.
options.html: been reported missing from Friday night.

questions.solution: The error lies in the part "been reported missing from Friday night." The error was in the use of "from" instead of "since" to indicate the starting point of the reported missing duration. "Since" is the appropriate term to use when referring to a specific starting time or point in the past. Correct sentence: Two border guards patrolling the nearby frontier with Georgia have also been reported missing since Friday night.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. A probe has been ordered / by the incident / that occurred at the celebration.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

A probe has been ordered / by the incident / that occurred at the celebration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'by the incident'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'for the incident' should be used instead of 'by the incident'.
  • We know that 'ordered for' means 'to use your position of authority to tell somebody to do something or to say that something must happen आदेश, आज्ञा या हुक्‍म देना'.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.
     

Correct Sentence: A probe has been ordered for the incident that occurred at the celebration.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहां 'by the incident' के स्थान पर 'for the incident' का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
  • हम जानते हैं कि 'ordered for' का अर्थ है 'किसी को कुछ करने के लिए कहने या यह कहने के लिए कि कुछ होना चाहिए' अपने अधिकार की स्थिति का उपयोग करना।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Avoid the puddles caused by the downpour was quite a problem while I was driving.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Avoid the puddles caused by the downpour was quite a problem while I was driving.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Avoid the puddles."

Key Points

  • Sentences always begin with a subject and not with a verb.
  • Here, Avoid is used which is a verb. The erroneous part “Avoid the puddles” should be “ Avoiding the puddles”.
  • Here, Avoiding is a gerund that makes the sentence grammatically correct.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 1. ​

Correct Sentence: Avoiding the puddles caused by the downpour was quite a problem while I was driving.


Additional Information

  • A Gerund is a non-finite verb that functions as a noun. It is formed by adding ‘ing’ with a verb. (verb-ing) A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence. The gerund always has the same function as a noun.
    • Example: Dancing is a good exercise.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. There was no denying the fact / that King Lear confided to / his daughter Cordelia / more than anybody else.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

There was no denying the fact / that King Lear confided to / his daughter Cordelia / more than anybody else.

options.text: There was no denying the fact
options.html: There was no denying the fact

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 1) i.e. 'that King Lear confided to.'

Key Points

  • The error lies in the part 'that King Lear confided to.'
  • The phrase "confided to" is not grammatically correct in this context.
  • The verb "confide" is usually followed by "in" when referring to a person.
  • The correct phrasing would be "that King Lear confided in."
  • The rest of the sentence is grammatically correct, and there are no errors in the other options.
  • Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'confided in' in place of 'confided to' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence: There was no denying the fact that King Lear confided in his daughter Cordelia more than anybody else.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are 21.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are 21.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 (able to drink).

Key Points

  • The phrase "able to drink" is incorrect in this context. The correct form is "not allowed to drink," as "able" implies physical capability, whereas the sentence intends to convey prohibition. (अनुमति नहीं है)
    • Example: You are not allowed to enter without a ticket.
  • The word "allowed" should be used here to indicate that someone is prohibited or restricted from doing something. (स्वीकृत नहीं है)
    • Example: She is not allowed to stay out late.
  • Therefore, the correct sentence is: "In some countries, you are not allowed to drink until you are 21."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 (able to drink).

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • In some countries, (कुछ देशों में,) This part of the sentence is correct and does not contain any errors.
    • Example: In some countries, it is customary to remove shoes before entering a home.
  • until you are 21. (जब तक आप 21 साल के नहीं हो जाते।) This part is grammatically correct.
    • Example: You cannot drive until you are 18.
  • you are not (आप नहीं हैं) This part is also grammatically correct.
    • Example: You are not allowed to bring pets into the restaurant.
